opening.text: Picture a narrow road that winds up a steep mountain. On one side is the rock wall. On the other side is a long drop. Along the road stand signs. Sharp curve ahead. Slow down. Falling rocks. Bridge out.

Now imagine a driver who says, I don't need signs. I know how to drive. I'll go my own way. We would worry about that driver. The signs are not there to spoil the trip. They are there because someone who has seen the whole road wants us to arrive safely.
The commandments are like those signs. God has seen the whole road. He knows every turn. And He puts up His signs because He loves the people on it.
Today I want to talk about obedience. It is a word that some people do not like. I hope we will see it in a new light.

mainMessage.text: Obedience is not about being controlled. It is about trust. When we obey, we are saying, Father, I believe You see more than I do. I will follow even when I cannot see the whole road.
And it is not about being perfect. It is about choosing, again and again, to do what He asks. Each choice builds faith, and faith makes the next choice easier.

We will look at six things. First, how obedience comes from love. Second, why God values it more than gifts. Third, what it takes to obey all the commandments. Fourth, why small choices matter. Fifth, why we follow the living prophets. And sixth, the joy that obedience brings.

blocks.text: The Savior gave a short and simple reason to obey. He did not say, because I am in charge. He said something much warmer.
If ye love me, keep my commandments.
That is the whole thing. Obedience is how love shows up in daily life. We do not obey to earn love. We obey because we already feel it.
The Lord also taught that His commandments are not random. Each one is tied to a blessing.

There is a law, irrevocably decreed in heaven before the foundations of this world, upon which all blessings are predicated—
And when we obtain any blessing from God, it is by obedience to that law upon which it is predicated.

Think of the road signs again. A sign that says slow down is tied to something real. A bridge, a curve, a cliff. The sign and the safety belong together. In the same way, each commandment is tied to a blessing that God wants us to have.
President Boyd K. Packer, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, put it simply. In his talk "The Balm of Gilead," from the October 1987 general conference, he said:
Obedience is powerful spiritual medicine. It comes close to being a cure-all.
A cure-all. That is a strong claim. But think about it. Many of our troubles come from not following what we already know. When we obey, we are often healed in ways we did not expect.
What does God want most from us? Not our gifts or our busy schedules. He wants our hearts.
Samuel said this to King Saul, who had offered a sacrifice in place of doing what the Lord commanded.

And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great a delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
To obey is better than sacrifice. Saul had a good reason for what he did, or so he thought. But the Lord did not want a gift instead of obedience. He wanted obedience.
The Lord also made a clear promise about how this works.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.

I, the Lord, am bound. That is a remarkable thing for God to say. When we do what He says, He is bound by His own word to bless us. It is a promise we can lean on. And the reverse is also true. If we do not, we have no promise to claim.
President Howard W. Hunter taught what the Lord loves most. In his talk "Commitment to God," from the October 1982 general conference, he said:
Surely the Lord loves, more than anything else, an unwavering determination to obey his counsel.
Unwavering determination. Not perfection. Not never failing. The Lord looks at our direction and our will. If we are set on obeying Him, He is pleased, even when we stumble on the way.
Sometimes we like some commandments better than others. It is easy to keep the ones that fit our day, and set aside the ones that ask more of us.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles gave a clear picture of this. In his talk "Face the Future with Faith," from the April 2011 general conference, he said:

\[You\] will encounter people who pick which commandments they will keep and ignore others that they choose to break. I call this the cafeteria approach to obedience. This practice of picking and choosing will not work. It will lead to misery. To prepare to meet God, one keeps all of His commandments. It takes faith to obey them, and keeping His commandments will strengthen that faith.

The cafeteria approach. We all know how that works. A little of this, none of that. But a road sign is only useful if we heed all of them. A driver who obeys the speed limit but ignores the bridge warning is not safe.
And notice the last line. It takes faith to obey. And obeying strengthens that faith. Faith and obedience feed each other.
Nephi showed us how this works. When his brothers murmured, he answered with trust.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.
He shall prepare a way. That is the promise behind every commandment. The Lord does not hand us a sign and leave us alone on the mountain. He prepares the way.
The young Ammonite warriors lived this too. Helaman wrote of them:

Yea, and they did obey and observe to perform every word of command with exactness; yea, and even according to their faith it was done unto them; and I did remember the words which they said unto me that their mothers had taught them.
Every word of command with exactness. And it was done unto them according to their faith. These young men were not perfect people. But they were people who trusted the One who gave the signs.
Most of the roads we travel are made of small steps. Obedience is the same. We do not become faithful in one great moment. We become faithful in many small ones.
Alma taught his son Helaman about this.

Now ye may suppose that this is foolishness in me; but behold I say unto you, that by small and simple things are great things brought to pass; and small means in many instances doth confound the wise.
And the Lord God doth work by means to bring about his great and eternal purposes; and by very small means the Lord doth confound the wise and bringeth about the salvation of many souls.
Small and simple things. A short prayer. A page of scripture. A kind word. A Sabbath kept. None of these will make the news. But great things are brought to pass by them.

President Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency taught why the small things matter. In his talk "Spiritual Preparedness: Start Early and Be Steady," from the October 2005 general conference, he said:

A loving Heavenly Father and His Beloved Son have given us all the help They can to pass the test of life set before us. But we must decide to obey and then do it. We build the faith to pass the tests of obedience over time and through our daily choices. We can decide now to do quickly whatever God asks of us. And we can decide to be steady in the small tests of obedience which build the faith to carry us through the great tests, which will surely come.

Start early. Be steady. Do quickly. These are good words for a driver on a mountain road. We cannot wait until we are at the edge of the cliff to decide whether to heed the sign. We decide long before, in the small daily choices. Then, when the great test comes, we are ready.
There is one more kind of sign. These are the signs held up by the Lord's servants, the prophets and apostles. They are the ones who can see farther down the road.
The Lord said this about His servants.

What I the Lord have spoken, I have spoken, and I excuse not myself; and though the heavens and the earth pass away, my word shall not pass away, but shall all be fulfilled, whether by mine own voice or by the voice of my servants, it is the same.
Whether by mine own voice or by the voice of my servants, it is the same. That is a great comfort. We do not have to guess what the Lord wants for us today. He speaks through living prophets.

Elder David R. Stone of the Seventy told of a hurricane that was coming toward a city in the Caribbean, and compared it to the storms of the spirit. In his talk "Spiritual Hurricanes," from the October 1999 general conference, he said:

But we also have our spiritual hurricane guardians, those whose calling it is to watch and warn, helping us avoid spiritual damage, destruction, and even death. Our watchmen on the tower are known to us as apostles and prophets. They are our spiritual eyes in the sky, and they know, through inspiration and insight and pure intelligence, the course these storms may take. They continue to raise their voices in warning to tell us of the tragic consequences of willful and wanton violations of the Lord's commandments. To intentionally ignore their warnings is to court misery, sorrow, and ruin. To follow them is to follow the chosen servants of the Lord into spiritual pastures of peace and plenty.
Spiritual eyes in the sky. They can see the storm before it reaches us. When they speak, it is not to control us. It is to protect us. And to follow them is to walk into peace and plenty.
Where does all this lead? To joy. That may be the greatest surprise about obedience.
The Savior spoke of this at the last supper.

If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
He obeyed His Father, and He abides in His love. He invites us to do the same, so that His joy may be in us. Not duty. Not weight. Joy.
King Benjamin said the same near the end of his great sermon.

And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. For behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual; and if they hold out faithful to the end they are received into heaven, that thereby they may dwell with God in a state of never-ending happiness. O remember, remember that these things are true; for the Lord God hath spoken it.
The blessed and happy state. That is where the mountain road leads, and it is worth the climb.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time they obeyed even though they did not understand why. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Noah builds the ark

blocks.text: Noah was asked to build a great ship, far from any sea, when no rain like that had ever fallen. People must have wondered about him. He did not have all the answers. He had a commandment. And he followed it.
Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.

According to all that God commanded him. Not part of it. Not the easy parts. All of it. And because he obeyed, his family was saved. Noah followed a sign long before the storm came, and that made all the difference.

application.text: Here are some steps for this week.
First, pick one sign. Think of one commandment that you have been keeping only some of the time. Decide to keep it fully this week.
Second, start small. Choose one small, daily act of obedience, like a morning prayer or a page of scripture. Do it every day for seven days.
Third, listen to the prophets. Read or watch one talk from the most recent general conference. Write down one thing the Lord is asking you to do through His servant, and do it.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God loves us and that His commandments are a gift. I know that when we follow them, He blesses us. I have felt the joy and peace that come from trying to do what He asks. I know that Jesus Christ kept every commandment and that He invites us to follow Him. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

closingVerse.text: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.

opening.text: My grandmother had a recipe for bread. It was written in pencil on a worn card. Flour, water, yeast, salt, and a little sugar. Knead it this long. Let it rise this long. Bake it at this heat.

One time someone tried to improve it. They left out the salt. They skipped the rising time. They turned the oven up to save a few minutes. The bread came out flat and hard. It looked nothing like hers.
The recipe was not a rule meant to limit anyone. It was the wisdom of a woman who had baked that bread a thousand times. She knew what worked.
God's commandments are like that. They come from One who knows exactly what makes a life rise, and what makes it fall flat.

mainMessage.text: Obedience means following the Lord's instructions, even when we would do it differently. It is built on trust. We trust that He knows the ingredients of a good life better than we do.
And it is a daily practice. We learn it the way a cook learns a recipe. By doing it again and again, until it becomes part of us.

In this talk we will look at six parts. First, the love behind obedience. Second, what the Lord values most. Third, why we cannot skip steps. Fourth, why small things matter. Fifth, why the Lord gives us prophets. And sixth, the joy at the end.

blocks.text: When Jesus talked about obeying Him, He tied it to something personal.
If ye love me, keep my commandments.
If ye love me. Not if you fear Me. Not if you must. Love is the starting place. A child who loves a parent wants to please them. We keep the commandments because we love the One who gave them.
And He told us there is a reason behind every instruction.

There is a law, irrevocably decreed in heaven before the foundations of this world, upon which all blessings are predicated—
And when we obtain any blessing from God, it is by obedience to that law upon which it is predicated.

Why does bread need yeast? Because yeast is what makes it rise. The rule and the result are connected. In the same way, each commandment is connected to a blessing. God did not make arbitrary rules. He built laws into how life works.
President Boyd K. Packer, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, spoke of the healing in this. In his talk "The Balm of Gilead," from the October 1987 general conference, he said:
Obedience is powerful spiritual medicine. It comes close to being a cure-all.
Medicine works only when we take it. We can read the label all day, but it will not help until we follow the directions. Obedience is the taking of the medicine.
Some people believe that if they do enough good things, they can skip the hard instructions. The scriptures speak plainly about this.
The prophet Samuel said it to King Saul.

And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great a delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.

Saul had kept the best of the animals to offer to the Lord. It sounded generous. But he had been told to do something different. Samuel told him that listening to God matters more than offering Him something else.
Like the cook who adds a favorite spice that is not in the recipe, we sometimes substitute our own ideas for what God asked. It may look good. But it is not what He asked.
The Lord gave a promise about what He does when we follow Him.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
He is bound. When we do what He says, He will keep His word. We can count on that every time.
President Howard W. Hunter taught what pleases the Lord. In his talk "Commitment to God," from the October 1982 general conference, he said:
Surely the Lord loves, more than anything else, an unwavering determination to obey his counsel.
Unwavering determination. That is what a good baker has. Even when the first loaf fails, they try again. The Lord is not asking for a flawless loaf. He is asking for a heart that keeps trying.
You cannot leave out half the ingredients and expect the bread to rise. The same is true of the commandments.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles warned about this. In his talk "Face the Future with Faith," from the April 2011 general conference, he said:

\[You\] will encounter people who pick which commandments they will keep and ignore others that they choose to break. I call this the cafeteria approach to obedience. This practice of picking and choosing will not work. It will lead to misery. To prepare to meet God, one keeps all of His commandments. It takes faith to obey them, and keeping His commandments will strengthen that faith.

Picking and choosing will not work. It is tempting, because some commandments are easy and others are not. But the recipe is one recipe. When we keep some and not others, we end up with something that does not match what God intended.
But look at the hopeful part. Keeping His commandments strengthens our faith. Each one we follow makes the next easier.
Nephi had this kind of faith, and he said it with confidence.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.
He shall prepare a way. The Lord never gives us a recipe without also giving us the means to follow it.
The young Ammonite soldiers were known for this kind of faith.

Yea, and they did obey and observe to perform every word of command with exactness; yea, and even according to their faith it was done unto them; and I did remember the words which they said unto me that their mothers had taught them.
Their mothers had taught them. These young men had learned to trust by watching those who loved them. Every word, with exactness. That is the kind of baker who makes bread that rises.
It only takes a pinch of salt. Yet without it, the whole loaf tastes flat. Small things often decide how a thing turns out.
Alma taught this to his son.

Now ye may suppose that this is foolishness in me; but behold I say unto you, that by small and simple things are great things brought to pass; and small means in many instances doth confound the wise.
And the Lord God doth work by means to bring about his great and eternal purposes; and by very small means the Lord doth confound the wise and bringeth about the salvation of many souls.

Small means. We may think that a quick prayer, a verse of scripture, or a small kindness does not count for much. The Lord says otherwise. By small and simple things, great things are brought to pass.
President Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency told us how this builds faith. In his talk "Spiritual Preparedness: Start Early and Be Steady," from the October 2005 general conference, he said:

A loving Heavenly Father and His Beloved Son have given us all the help They can to pass the test of life set before us. But we must decide to obey and then do it. We build the faith to pass the tests of obedience over time and through our daily choices. We can decide now to do quickly whatever God asks of us. And we can decide to be steady in the small tests of obedience which build the faith to carry us through the great tests, which will surely come.
He says the same thing a good baker would. You do not wait for the day of the big dinner to learn to bake. You practice every week. Then, when the day comes, your hands know what to do.
A good recipe is passed down by someone who has made it many times. In the same way, the Lord gives us living prophets who can guide us today.

What I the Lord have spoken, I have spoken, and I excuse not myself; and though the heavens and the earth pass away, my word shall not pass away, but shall all be fulfilled, whether by mine own voice or by the voice of my servants, it is the same.
When the prophets speak by the Spirit, it is the same as if the Lord spoke. That is a remarkable gift. We are not left to work it out alone.
Elder David R. Stone of the Seventy described what prophets do for us. In his talk "Spiritual Hurricanes," from the October 1999 general conference, he said:

But we also have our spiritual hurricane guardians, those whose calling it is to watch and warn, helping us avoid spiritual damage, destruction, and even death. Our watchmen on the tower are known to us as apostles and prophets. They are our spiritual eyes in the sky, and they know, through inspiration and insight and pure intelligence, the course these storms may take. They continue to raise their voices in warning to tell us of the tragic consequences of willful and wanton violations of the Lord's commandments. To intentionally ignore their warnings is to court misery, sorrow, and ruin. To follow them is to follow the chosen servants of the Lord into spiritual pastures of peace and plenty.
Watchmen on the tower. They are looking out for us. When they give a warning, it is because they love us and they can see what is coming. And when we follow, we find peace and plenty.
And what is the fruit of all this? The Savior calls it joy.

If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.

A full joy. That is what He wants for us. Think of a kitchen filled with the smell of fresh bread and a family gathered at the table. That is a picture of a life where the Lord's instructions have been followed.
King Benjamin spoke of the same blessing.

And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. For behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual; and if they hold out faithful to the end they are received into heaven, that thereby they may dwell with God in a state of never-ending happiness. O remember, remember that these things are true; for the Lord God hath spoken it.
Blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual. Never-ending happiness. That is a table worth sitting down to.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time they followed an instruction and saw the result. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Nephi and the plates

blocks.text: Nephi and his brothers returned to Jerusalem to get the brass plates. They had tried and failed. Nephi went alone, in the night, into the city. He had no plan. He only had the commandment and his faith that the Lord would prepare a way.
And I was led by the Spirit, not knowing beforehand the things which I should do.

Not knowing beforehand. That is what obedience often feels like. We have the instruction, but not the whole picture. Nephi took the first step, and the Spirit showed him the next one. That is how the recipe is followed, one step at a time.

application.text: Here are some steps for this week.
First, read the recipe. Spend ten minutes reading the commandments or a talk about one of them. Ask what the Lord is teaching.
Second, keep the whole recipe. Choose one commandment you tend to skip. This week, keep it fully and see what happens.
Third, take the next step. Is there something the Lord has asked you to do that you do not fully understand? Take one step, like Nephi, and trust that the Spirit will show you the next.

closingVerse.text: Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations;

opening.text: A train is a heavy machine. It can pull a hundred cars across a whole country. But it can only do that on one thing. The track.
Take a train off its track and what do you have? A very large, very heavy problem. The track does not limit the train. It is what lets the train go anywhere at all.
Some people think the commandments are like fences. They keep us in. But I think they are more like rails. They are what carry us forward, farther and faster than we could go on our own.
Today we will talk about obedience, and why the Lord's rails are a gift.

mainMessage.text: When we choose to obey, we choose to stay on the track that leads home. It is not always the easiest ground. But it is the one that goes where we want to go.
Obedience is not a cold word. It begins with love and ends with joy. In between, it asks us to trust God when we cannot see the end of the line.

We will look at six things. First, why we obey. Second, what God prizes. Third, why we keep the whole track and not just part. Fourth, why the small spikes matter. Fifth, how prophets guide the way. And sixth, where the track leads.

blocks.text: Why do we stay on the track? Jesus gave the reason in one short line.
If ye love me, keep my commandments.
It starts with love. We do not obey out of fear of being punished. We obey because we love Him and want to be with Him.
He also taught that each commandment is connected to a blessing.

There is a law, irrevocably decreed in heaven before the foundations of this world, upon which all blessings are predicated—
And when we obtain any blessing from God, it is by obedience to that law upon which it is predicated.

Predicated is an old word. It means based on. Every blessing rests on a law. The track rests on the ground beneath it, and the train rests on the track. If we want the blessing, we stay on the law that carries it.
President Boyd K. Packer, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, spoke of the healing power of this. In his talk "The Balm of Gilead," from the October 1987 general conference, he said:
Obedience is powerful spiritual medicine. It comes close to being a cure-all.
Many of us carry burdens that we have tried to fix in complicated ways. Often the answer is simpler. We go back to the track.
What does God prize? Surprisingly, it is not our impressive offerings. It is our willingness to follow.
The prophet Samuel spoke to King Saul after Saul had gone his own way.

And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great a delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
Saul was a king. He could have done many grand things for God. But grand things do not make up for leaving the track. The Lord wanted him to listen.
The Lord has also told us what happens on both sides of this choice.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
There is a promise on the track. When we do what He says, He is bound. Off the track, there is no promise. It is that clear.
President Howard W. Hunter explained what the Lord looks for. In his talk "Commitment to God," from the October 1982 general conference, he said:
Surely the Lord loves, more than anything else, an unwavering determination to obey his counsel.
An engine does not need to be fast to stay on the track. It needs to keep going the right way. The Lord loves our determination. It is the steady setting of our will, day after day.
A track with gaps is not a track. A train will not cross a broken bridge. Yet some of us try to keep part of the commandments and skip others.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles named it. In his talk "Face the Future with Faith," from the April 2011 general conference, he said:

\[You\] will encounter people who pick which commandments they will keep and ignore others that they choose to break. I call this the cafeteria approach to obedience. This practice of picking and choosing will not work. It will lead to misery. To prepare to meet God, one keeps all of His commandments. It takes faith to obey them, and keeping His commandments will strengthen that faith.

It will not work. That is plain talk, and it is meant kindly. It is a warning from someone who has seen where a broken track leads. But the end of his statement is a promise. Keeping the commandments strengthens our faith. The more we stay on the rails, the more we trust them.
Nephi trusted them. He said this when the task seemed too big.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.
He shall prepare a way. Railroad builders lay track across mountains and rivers. The Lord does the same for us. He builds the way before we get there.
And Helaman's young soldiers followed this way.

Yea, and they did obey and observe to perform every word of command with exactness; yea, and even according to their faith it was done unto them; and I did remember the words which they said unto me that their mothers had taught them.
Every word. With exactness. Not part of the track. All of it. And it was done to them according to their faith.
A railroad is held together by thousands of small spikes. No one notices them. But if enough of them work loose, the train can derail.
Alma taught us about small things.

Now ye may suppose that this is foolishness in me; but behold I say unto you, that by small and simple things are great things brought to pass; and small means in many instances doth confound the wise.
And the Lord God doth work by means to bring about his great and eternal purposes; and by very small means the Lord doth confound the wise and bringeth about the salvation of many souls.

By very small means. Our daily habits are the spikes. Praying each day. Reading the word. Keeping the Sabbath. Paying tithing. Being honest in small things. None of them look big. But they hold the track together.

President Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency described how these small things carry us through the big tests. In his talk "Spiritual Preparedness: Start Early and Be Steady," from the October 2005 general conference, he said:

A loving Heavenly Father and His Beloved Son have given us all the help They can to pass the test of life set before us. But we must decide to obey and then do it. We build the faith to pass the tests of obedience over time and through our daily choices. We can decide now to do quickly whatever God asks of us. And we can decide to be steady in the small tests of obedience which build the faith to carry us through the great tests, which will surely come.
The great tests will surely come. A train does not wait for a storm to check its track. The track must be sound before the storm arrives. Our daily choices make it sound.
A train has a person at the front who watches the track ahead. In the Lord's kingdom, the prophets and apostles do something similar.

What I the Lord have spoken, I have spoken, and I excuse not myself; and though the heavens and the earth pass away, my word shall not pass away, but shall all be fulfilled, whether by mine own voice or by the voice of my servants, it is the same.
It is the same. The words of the Lord's servants, when given by the Spirit, carry His voice. That means we do not have to guess which way the track bends.
Elder David R. Stone of the Seventy spoke of how the prophets watch for danger. In his talk "Spiritual Hurricanes," from the October 1999 general conference, he said:

But we also have our spiritual hurricane guardians, those whose calling it is to watch and warn, helping us avoid spiritual damage, destruction, and even death. Our watchmen on the tower are known to us as apostles and prophets. They are our spiritual eyes in the sky, and they know, through inspiration and insight and pure intelligence, the course these storms may take. They continue to raise their voices in warning to tell us of the tragic consequences of willful and wanton violations of the Lord's commandments. To intentionally ignore their warnings is to court misery, sorrow, and ruin. To follow them is to follow the chosen servants of the Lord into spiritual pastures of peace and plenty.
Spiritual pastures of peace and plenty. That is the destination of the line. And the prophets point us toward it.
Where does the track end? At a place of joy.

If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
Why did Jesus say all of this? So that His joy might remain in us, and our joy might be full. The whole purpose of the commandments is joy.
King Benjamin reminded his people of the same truth.

And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. For behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual; and if they hold out faithful to the end they are received into heaven, that thereby they may dwell with God in a state of never-ending happiness. O remember, remember that these things are true; for the Lord God hath spoken it.
If they hold out faithful to the end. The train rides all the way home. And there, God waits in a state of never-ending happiness.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time they stayed on the track when it was hard. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Abraham rises early

blocks.text: God asked Abraham to do the hardest thing a father could be asked. To offer his son Isaac. Abraham did not argue. He did not wait. The scripture tells us what he did.

And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went unto the place of which God had told him.

Rose up early in the morning. He did not delay. He prepared, and he went. Abraham did not know how this would turn out. He only knew that God had asked. His obedience was quick and full, and God honored it. The Lord provided a way, as He always does.

application.text: Here are some steps for this week.
First, check your track. Ask yourself, which commandment am I most likely to skip? Write it down. This week, keep it.
Second, tighten the spikes. Choose two small daily habits, such as prayer and scripture reading. Do both every day this week, no matter how busy you are.
Third, rise up early. When the Lord prompts you to do something, do it quickly. Do not wait for a better time.

closingVerse.text: If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.

opening.text: Before every flight, a pilot runs through a checklist. It does not matter how many years they have flown. It does not matter how many thousands of hours they have logged. They still read the list, item by item, out loud.

Why? Because the list was written by people who learned from mistakes. Each line on it exists because, at some point, skipping that step cost something. The best pilots are not the ones who think they are too skilled for the list. They are the ones who follow it every time.
The Lord has given us a checklist too. We call them commandments. They were not written to slow us down. They were given by One who sees what we cannot, and who wants us to land safely.
Let us talk about what it means to follow them.

mainMessage.text: Obedience is trust in action. We do what God asks, step by step, because we believe He knows what we do not. And as we do, our trust grows.
It is also a daily choice. A good pilot does not decide once to follow the list. They follow it every time they fly. We do the same, one day at a time.

We will look at six things. First, the love behind the commandments. Second, what God values most. Third, why we cannot choose only some. Fourth, how small steps prepare us for large trials. Fifth, how prophets help us see ahead. And sixth, the joy that comes.

blocks.text: The Savior told us why we keep His commandments, and it is not what some people expect.
If ye love me, keep my commandments.
Love comes first. A pilot who loves the passengers will not skip the checklist. A disciple who loves the Lord will not skip His word.
The Lord taught that every commandment is tied to a result.

There is a law, irrevocably decreed in heaven before the foundations of this world, upon which all blessings are predicated—
And when we obtain any blessing from God, it is by obedience to that law upon which it is predicated.

There is a law behind every blessing. Lift comes from the shape of the wing. Safety comes from the steps in the list. In the same way, blessings come from the laws God has set. We cannot receive the blessing and ignore the law it rests on.
President Boyd K. Packer, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, described what obedience does for us. In his talk "The Balm of Gilead," from the October 1987 general conference, he said:
Obedience is powerful spiritual medicine. It comes close to being a cure-all.
So many of our problems have a spiritual root. And obedience, simple and steady, reaches down to that root.
What does the Lord value more than anything we can give Him? The answer may surprise you.
Samuel told King Saul.

And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great a delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
To hearken. To listen and then act. It is better than the greatest offering. A pilot who impresses the crowd with fancy flying but ignores the tower will not last long. The one who listens does.
The Lord made a promise about this.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
When we do what He says, He is bound to bless us. That is a promise we can build on. It is as firm as the ground.
President Howard W. Hunter named what the Lord loves. In his talk "Commitment to God," from the October 1982 general conference, he said:
Surely the Lord loves, more than anything else, an unwavering determination to obey his counsel.
Unwavering. It means steady. A good pilot holds the heading even when the wind pushes. We hold our course in the same way, by determination.
A pilot cannot decide to skip the fuel check because it seems small. Every item on the list matters. The same is true of the commandments.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles gave us a warning. In his talk "Face the Future with Faith," from the April 2011 general conference, he said:

\[You\] will encounter people who pick which commandments they will keep and ignore others that they choose to break. I call this the cafeteria approach to obedience. This practice of picking and choosing will not work. It will lead to misery. To prepare to meet God, one keeps all of His commandments. It takes faith to obey them, and keeping His commandments will strengthen that faith.

It will lead to misery. That is a hard sentence. But it is true. A flight with one skipped check is a flight at risk. A life with one ignored commandment is a life carrying weight we did not need to carry.
Then comes the good news. Obeying builds faith. Each step makes the next one easier.
Nephi trusted this way. He told his father:

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.
He shall prepare a way. The Lord does not give us a checklist and then leave us. He goes with us through every step.
The stripling warriors lived this too.

Yea, and they did obey and observe to perform every word of command with exactness; yea, and even according to their faith it was done unto them; and I did remember the words which they said unto me that their mothers had taught them.
With exactness. They did not edit the instructions. They followed them as they were given.
Pilots practice in simulators long before they face a real emergency. They run through small drills again and again. When the real thing comes, their hands know what to do.
Alma taught his son the same idea.

Now ye may suppose that this is foolishness in me; but behold I say unto you, that by small and simple things are great things brought to pass; and small means in many instances doth confound the wise.
And the Lord God doth work by means to bring about his great and eternal purposes; and by very small means the Lord doth confound the wise and bringeth about the salvation of many souls.
Small means. A prayer said in the morning. A scripture read at night. A promise kept when no one is watching. Drills, in a way. They look small. But they prepare us for the day of testing.
President Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency taught this. In his talk "Spiritual Preparedness: Start Early and Be Steady," from the October 2005 general conference, he said:

A loving Heavenly Father and His Beloved Son have given us all the help They can to pass the test of life set before us. But we must decide to obey and then do it. We build the faith to pass the tests of obedience over time and through our daily choices. We can decide now to do quickly whatever God asks of us. And we can decide to be steady in the small tests of obedience which build the faith to carry us through the great tests, which will surely come.
Decide now. Do quickly. Be steady. If we wait until the emergency to start practicing, it is late. But if we practice now, we will be ready.
A pilot is guided by the control tower, which can see the whole sky. The Lord has placed guides for us too.

What I the Lord have spoken, I have spoken, and I excuse not myself; and though the heavens and the earth pass away, my word shall not pass away, but shall all be fulfilled, whether by mine own voice or by the voice of my servants, it is the same.
By the voice of my servants, it is the same. When they speak as moved by the Spirit, we are hearing the Lord. A pilot who ignores the tower is in danger. A member who ignores the prophets is too.
Elder David R. Stone of the Seventy taught this clearly. In his talk "Spiritual Hurricanes," from the October 1999 general conference, he said:

But we also have our spiritual hurricane guardians, those whose calling it is to watch and warn, helping us avoid spiritual damage, destruction, and even death. Our watchmen on the tower are known to us as apostles and prophets. They are our spiritual eyes in the sky, and they know, through inspiration and insight and pure intelligence, the course these storms may take. They continue to raise their voices in warning to tell us of the tragic consequences of willful and wanton violations of the Lord's commandments. To intentionally ignore their warnings is to court misery, sorrow, and ruin. To follow them is to follow the chosen servants of the Lord into spiritual pastures of peace and plenty.
Watchmen on the tower. That is exactly their role. They see the weather ahead. They warn us out of love. And when we follow, we land in peace.
The goal of every flight is a safe landing, and for the faithful, that is joy.

If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
Abide in my love. That is where obedience leads. We stay near Him, and His joy stays with us.
King Benjamin pointed to the same destination.

And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. For behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual; and if they hold out faithful to the end they are received into heaven, that thereby they may dwell with God in a state of never-ending happiness. O remember, remember that these things are true; for the Lord God hath spoken it.
Heaven, and never-ending happiness. That is the destination we are flying toward.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time they followed an instruction that did not make sense at first. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Joshua and the walls of Jericho

blocks.text: The Lord told Joshua how to take the city of Jericho. March around the walls once a day for six days. On the seventh day, march around seven times, blow the trumpets, and shout. It was not how armies fight. It must have sounded strange. But the people did exactly as they were told.

So the people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets: and it came to pass, when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, and the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city.
The wall fell down flat. Not because of strength, but because of obedience. The people followed instructions that did not look like a plan. They trusted God, and He did the work.

First, read your checklist. Spend a few minutes listing the commandments you are trying to live. Mark any that you have been letting slide.
Second, practice a drill. Choose one small act, like a daily prayer at the same time each day, and keep it for the whole week.
Third, listen to the tower. Find the most recent message from the prophet or the apostles. Read it, and choose one thing to do.

closingVerse.text: Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.

opening.text: A grape vine left to itself will sprawl on the ground. Its leaves get dirty. Its fruit gets small and sour. But give that same vine a trellis, and it climbs. It reaches the sun. It grows heavy with sweet grapes.
The vine does not lose anything by the trellis. It gains. The wood and wire do not hold it back. They hold it up.
I think the commandments work this way. They are not a cage. They are a trellis. They give our lives something to climb, so that we can grow toward the light.
Today we will talk about obedience, and how it helps us grow.

mainMessage.text: We obey because we love God and because we trust that His way leads to life. The commandments lift us. They give shape to our growth.
Obedience is also a path to freedom. A vine on a trellis can reach the sun. A person who follows the Lord's way is free from many things that bind others.

We will look at six things. First, the love at the root. Second, what the Lord wants from us. Third, why we keep all of it. Fourth, how small acts help us grow. Fifth, how prophets guide us. And sixth, the fruit that comes.

blocks.text: Jesus told us what lies at the root of obedience.
If ye love me, keep my commandments.
It begins with love. The vine grows toward the one who gives it light. We grow toward the Lord because we love Him.
He also revealed that blessings are tied to laws.

There is a law, irrevocably decreed in heaven before the foundations of this world, upon which all blessings are predicated—
And when we obtain any blessing from God, it is by obedience to that law upon which it is predicated.

There is a law of growth. Water, sun, and support. A gardener does not make it up. They learn it and follow it. In the same way, the Lord has told us the laws of spiritual growth, and when we follow them, we receive the blessing.
President Boyd K. Packer, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, spoke of what this does for us. In his talk "The Balm of Gilead," from the October 1987 general conference, he said:
Obedience is powerful spiritual medicine. It comes close to being a cure-all.
A sick vine is often helped by simple things. Good soil, water, and a trellis. A weary soul is often helped by simple things too. Obedience is one of the best.
The Lord does not want a showy offering. He wants a listening heart.
That is what Samuel told Saul.

And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great a delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
To obey is better than sacrifice. A gardener would rather see a vine climb than receive a bouquet from it. The Lord wants us to grow in the way He designed.
He also made us a promise.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
When we follow, He is bound to bless. That is our assurance. We can build on it.
President Howard W. Hunter taught what pleases Him. In his talk "Commitment to God," from the October 1982 general conference, he said:
Surely the Lord loves, more than anything else, an unwavering determination to obey his counsel.
Unwavering. Like a vine that keeps reaching up, even after a storm bends it. The Lord loves that kind of determination.
A vine cannot choose to climb only part of the way. If the trellis is half built, the vine falls back. The same is true of our obedience.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles spoke of this. In his talk "Face the Future with Faith," from the April 2011 general conference, he said:

\[You\] will encounter people who pick which commandments they will keep and ignore others that they choose to break. I call this the cafeteria approach to obedience. This practice of picking and choosing will not work. It will lead to misery. To prepare to meet God, one keeps all of His commandments. It takes faith to obey them, and keeping His commandments will strengthen that faith.
Picking and choosing. We may not mean to do it. We simply find some commandments easier than others. But the trellis only works when every part is in place.
The encouraging part is the last line. Keeping His commandments strengthens our faith. We do not need to be strong first. We become strong as we climb.
Nephi gave us a great example.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.
A way is prepared. The trellis is already in place when the vine starts to grow. The Lord has built it before we begin.
And the young warriors of Helaman followed it.

Yea, and they did obey and observe to perform every word of command with exactness; yea, and even according to their faith it was done unto them; and I did remember the words which they said unto me that their mothers had taught them.
Their mothers had taught them, and they held to it. Their faith had a good trellis to climb.
A vine does not climb in a day. It grows a little each morning. Over a season, those small inches become a canopy.
Alma taught his son about this kind of growth.

Now ye may suppose that this is foolishness in me; but behold I say unto you, that by small and simple things are great things brought to pass; and small means in many instances doth confound the wise.
And the Lord God doth work by means to bring about his great and eternal purposes; and by very small means the Lord doth confound the wise and bringeth about the salvation of many souls.
Small and simple things. A little each day. That is how a life of faith is built. We do not need dramatic moments. We need faithful ones.
President Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency taught this clearly. In his talk "Spiritual Preparedness: Start Early and Be Steady," from the October 2005 general conference, he said:

A loving Heavenly Father and His Beloved Son have given us all the help They can to pass the test of life set before us. But we must decide to obey and then do it. We build the faith to pass the tests of obedience over time and through our daily choices. We can decide now to do quickly whatever God asks of us. And we can decide to be steady in the small tests of obedience which build the faith to carry us through the great tests, which will surely come.

Over time and through our daily choices. That is the pattern. A vine with deep roots and a firm hold on its trellis can face the winds. The great tests will surely come, and the faith we built in small ways will hold.
A gardener knows the vine better than the vine knows itself. The Lord knows us better than we know ourselves. He gives us prophets to show us how to grow.

What I the Lord have spoken, I have spoken, and I excuse not myself; and though the heavens and the earth pass away, my word shall not pass away, but shall all be fulfilled, whether by mine own voice or by the voice of my servants, it is the same.
The voice of my servants. It is the same. This is a great gift. We can trust the guidance that comes from the Lord's chosen leaders.
Elder David R. Stone of the Seventy taught how prophets protect us. In his talk "Spiritual Hurricanes," from the October 1999 general conference, he said:

But we also have our spiritual hurricane guardians, those whose calling it is to watch and warn, helping us avoid spiritual damage, destruction, and even death. Our watchmen on the tower are known to us as apostles and prophets. They are our spiritual eyes in the sky, and they know, through inspiration and insight and pure intelligence, the course these storms may take. They continue to raise their voices in warning to tell us of the tragic consequences of willful and wanton violations of the Lord's commandments. To intentionally ignore their warnings is to court misery, sorrow, and ruin. To follow them is to follow the chosen servants of the Lord into spiritual pastures of peace and plenty.
A gardener sees the storm coming and ties the vine tighter to the trellis. The prophets do the same for us. They warn so that we can hold fast. And in the end, we find pastures of peace and plenty.
And what is the fruit? Joy, which the Savior wants for each of us.

If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
In the same chapter, Jesus speaks of the vine and the branches. He says we must abide in Him. To abide is to stay close. When we keep His commandments, we stay close, and His joy remains in us.
King Benjamin spoke of this fruit as well.

And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. For behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual; and if they hold out faithful to the end they are received into heaven, that thereby they may dwell with God in a state of never-ending happiness. O remember, remember that these things are true; for the Lord God hath spoken it.
Blessed and happy. That is what a life well-grown looks like.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time they did something simply because the Lord asked. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The wedding at Cana

blocks.text: At a wedding in Cana, the family ran out of wine. Mary told the servants to go to her son. She gave them one instruction.

His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.
And there were set there six waterpots of stone, after the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three firkins apiece.
Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.
And he saith unto them, Draw out now, and bear unto the governor of the feast. And they bare it.

The servants were asked to fill jars with water. It was an odd request when what was needed was wine. But they filled them up to the brim. Not halfway. And then they did the next thing He asked. The water became wine. They did not understand how, but they did what they were told. And they were part of the miracle.

application.text: Here are some steps for this week.
First, build your trellis. Write down three daily habits that help you grow spiritually. Keep all three for the whole week.
Second, fill the jars to the brim. Think of one thing the Lord has asked of you that you have only done halfway. This week, do it fully.
Third, follow the guide. Read a recent talk from a prophet or apostle. Ask the Lord what He wants you to do with it, and act on the answer.

blocks.text: I know that the Lord's commandments are a gift, and that they help us grow. I know that when we do what He asks, even small things, He does great things with them. I have felt joy that comes from following Him. I know that Jesus Christ is the true vine, and that He invites us to abide in Him. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

I invite you to do fully one thing the Lord has asked that you have done only halfway.
I invite you to read a recent talk from a prophet or apostle and act on what you learn.

closingVerse.text: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.
